title: Unitree Prices Shanghai IPO at $9 Billion Valuation
summary: Unitree Robotics priced its initial public offering on Shanghai's STAR Market at 150.80 yuan ($22.34) per share on August 6, 2026, valuing the company at roughly 61 billion yuan ($9.04 billion). The Hangzhou-based maker of humanoid and quadruped robots is selling about 40.45 million new shares, 10% of its enlarged share capital, to raise 6.1 billion yuan, making it China's first mainland-listed humanoid robot maker. Nine strategic placement investors joined the offering, including DeepSeek's parent company, Tencent, PetroChina and China Southern Power Grid. IPO subscriptions open August 10, with proceeds earmarked for robot AI model R&D, new products and a manufacturing base. Unitree's 2025 revenue more than quadrupled to 1.7 billion yuan, with humanoid robots overtaking quadrupeds as its largest business line at 867.8 million yuan.
whyItMatters: Unitree's listing is a landmark event for the humanoid robotics industry, giving public markets their first direct, mainland-Chinese pure-play on humanoid robots and testing investor appetite for a sector still without profitable at-scale deployment. Bringing in AI labs like DeepSeek as strategic investors also signals a push to fuse frontier foundation models with Unitree's hardware, a bet that embodied intelligence and general-purpose AI will co-evolve just as U.S.-China trade tensions threaten Unitree's access to American customers for future robot models.
